::: {.lede}
Two strands of work: a PhD project on the behavioural drivers of epidemic
dynamics, and, part-time, the economic evaluation of blood-borne virus
screening.
:::

## Interests

- Infectious disease modelling
- Machine learning
- Social contact, mobility and attitude data
- Economic evaluation

## PhD project

### Behavioural drivers of epidemic dynamics

Social contact, mobility and attitude data carry signal about how people
actually behave during an outbreak — who mixes with whom, how that changes under
pressure, and how quickly it reverts. The question is whether that signal can be
used not just to explain epidemic dynamics after the fact, but to help
anticipate them.

## Alongside it

### Economic evaluation of blood-borne virus screening

An NIHR-funded project on the cost-effectiveness of blood-borne virus testing
interventions: hepatitis B progression modelling for emergency department
opt-out testing; TB IGRA testing in high-risk groups; and micro-costing of
digitally enhanced testing.

## Earlier work

### Vaccine responses and vaccine equity

Finished work: machine learning to understand vaccine responses to influenza,
and modelling of vaccine equity and trachoma resurgence.
